definitions.explanation: Being appointed to a position for a second or subsequent time after having previously held and left it. Used for political leaders, corporate executives, and organizational officers.

examples.japanese: {社長|しゃちょう}が{再就任|さいしゅうにん}することになった。
examples.english: The company president will be reappointed.

examples.japanese: {前|ぜん}CEO の{再就任|さいしゅうにん}を{求|もと}める{声|こえ}が{高|たか}まっている。
examples.english: Calls for the reappointment of the former CEO are growing louder.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{一度|いちど}{辞任|じにん}したが、{組織|そしき}の{立|た}て{直|なお}しのために{再就任|さいしゅうにん}を{引|ひ}き{受|う}けた。
examples.english: He resigned once but accepted reappointment in order to rebuild the organization.

notes:
Composed of {再|さい} (again/re-) and {就任|しゅうにん} (assuming office). Describes the act of taking up a position that one previously held. The prefix {再|さい} productively attaches to many action nouns to add the meaning of "again."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {再就任|さいしゅうにん}する: to be reappointed
- {再就任|さいしゅうにん}を{果|は}たす: to achieve reappointment
- {再就任|さいしゅうにん}を{要請|ようせい}する: to request reappointment

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {再任|さいにん}: reappointment — a shorter synonym, often used in official contexts
- {就任|しゅうにん}: assumption of office — the base word, first appointment
- {復帰|ふっき}: return — broader, can apply to returning to any role or activity
- {辞任|じにん}: resignation — the act of leaving a position
